fields.meta_title: Win Loss Survey Builder for Sales Teams | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a win loss survey from a prompt: send it when a deal closes, ask won and lost buyers different questions, and keep each answer.
fields.h1: Build a Win Loss Survey and Learn Why Deals Were Won or Lost
fields.hero_description: Build a win loss survey that goes out when a deal closes, asks the buyer why, and saves each answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into Your Win Loss Survey
fields.features_subheading: The survey a buyer sees after a deal closes, and what happens to their answers once they submit.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from how you sell

Describe what you sell, who buys it, and the vendors you lose to. Emergent drafts the survey and its logic from that prompt, and a follow-up prompt changes any question.
fields.feature_2:
Sent when the deal closes in your CRM

The app connects to your CRM through its API. When a deal moves to closed won or closed lost, the buyer gets the survey, and the answers come back tied to that deal.
fields.feature_3:
Separate paths for won and lost buyers

A buyer who chose you is asked what tipped the decision. A buyer who went elsewhere is asked which vendor won and why. Nobody sees questions meant for the other side.
fields.feature_4:
A short survey, one screen at a time

Buyers answer one question per screen, so a ranking of five reasons and an open text box never crowd one phone screen. The buyer only reads the question in front of them.
fields.feature_5:
Hard losses go to a named person

Set a rule for the losses you want to hear about first, such as large deals. The app emails those answers to the person you choose, or sends them a Slack direct message.
fields.feature_6:
Answers stored with the deal

Each answer is a row in a database you own, with the deal, its value, the outcome, and the date. Responses have no cap, and paid plans export the full code to GitHub.

fields.tab_content_1:
19 lost deals with one reason: setup time

Lumenfield Analytics sends a short survey whenever a deal is marked closed lost in its CRM. Last quarter, 46 lost buyers answered. Setup time was the main reason for 19 of them, ahead of price at 11 and a missing integration at 9, with 7 giving other reasons. Lumenfield now puts a setup plan in every proposal.
fields.tab_content_2:
For 17 won buyers, dispatch fit came first

Brindlemark asked 38 buyers who chose its freight routing software to rank five reasons for the decision. Fit with their dispatch system came first for 17 of them, and price came first for 8. The sales team now opens every demo with the dispatch connection instead of the price sheet.
fields.tab_content_3:
When a bid over $40,000 is lost, Coralie gets the answers

Quillmoor Solar emails the survey answers from every lost bid over $40,000 to Coralie, its sales director. A $62,000 warehouse roof bid came back lost: the buyer picked an installer who could start in 3 weeks, against Quillmoor's 8. Coralie called the buyer the next morning.
fields.tab_content_4:
14 of 52 buyers agree to a call

Tarnwick Labs ends its survey by asking whether the buyer would take a 20-minute call. Of the 52 buyers who answered this quarter, 21 won and 31 lost, 14 said yes, and 8 of those came from lost deals. Their names and answers go onto the product marketing team's call list.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Win Loss Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a win loss survey that shows why buyers chose you or went elsewhere, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Choose which deals get the survey
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Split the won and lost questions
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the decisions the survey will feed, such as the demo script or the proposal template. Write down two or three goals, and cut any question that serves none of them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Send it to won and lost deals alike. The comparison between the two groups is the point. If you close a lot of small deals, set a floor by deal value and keep it the same all quarter.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Forrester advises win/loss surveys of less than 5 minutes. Its suggested format is ranking questions on capabilities, pricing, sales effectiveness, and company sentiment, plus one open-ended question.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask won buyers what tipped the decision. Ask lost buyers which vendor they chose and the main reason. Give each reason list an Other option with a text box for anything you missed.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Send it soon after the decision
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the survey within days of the decision, while the buyer still remembers the details. Tie it to the deal stage in your CRM, and send it under the sales rep's name, not a no-reply address.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it on three recent deals
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before the full send, run the survey on three recent deals, two lost and one won. Check that each buyer sees only their own path and that every answer lands next to the right deal.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Tally the main reasons once a quarter and compare them with the last one. Change one thing at a time, such as the proposal, and let the next quarter's answers show whether it worked.

faq_plan.q: What is a win loss survey?
faq_plan.a: A win loss survey is a short questionnaire sent to a buyer after they decide, asking why they chose you or another vendor. Klue defines it as a structured questionnaire that helps you understand why buyers chose you (or didn't) right after they make their decision. Won deals show what to protect, and lost deals show what to fix.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a win loss survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe your sales process and the deals you want to hear from in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder. It builds the survey with one path for won buyers and another for lost ones, plus the database the answers go into. Connect your CRM through its API to send the survey as each deal closes, and run it on a few recent deals before you switch it on.

faq_plan.q: What win loss survey questions should I ask a buyer who chose a competitor?
faq_plan.a: Ask which vendor they picked and the single main reason, from a short list with an Other option. Then ask them to rate your product, your price, and your sales process against the vendor they chose. Close with one open question: what would have changed your decision? Keep open questions few, since each one asks the buyer to write.

faq_plan.q: Should a win loss survey go to buyers who said yes, or only to lost deals?
faq_plan.a: Send it to both. Won buyers tell you which strengths closed the deal, and that is the list to protect when you change your pricing or your demo. Keep the questions about the buying decision itself. Once the buyer is a customer, questions about using the product belong in a customer feedback survey.

faq_plan.q: How soon after a deal closes should a win loss survey go out?
faq_plan.a: As soon as the decision is made. Forrester advises short, automated surveys sent right after each deal closes, and Klue's guidance is to send within 30 days while memory is fresh. Pick one delay for every deal and keep it, and the answers from different months stay comparable.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a win loss survey have?
faq_plan.a: There is no set number: let the time limit decide. Time a colleague taking the survey on a phone, and cut questions until it runs under 5 minutes. Ranking questions are quick to answer. Each open question asks the buyer to write, and one or two of those is enough. A survey Emergent builds can show one question per screen, which keeps a long ranking readable on a small screen.

faq_plan.q: Can a business that sells to consumers use a win loss survey?
faq_plan.a: Yes, wherever a customer compares your quote with someone else's and then decides. A caterer that loses a wedding booking can ask the same two things: who did you choose, and why? Describe that booking process in your prompt, and Emergent builds the survey around it. Where there is no quote to win or lose, such as diners after a meal, a restaurant survey fits better.

faq_plan.q: Does a win loss survey need an incentive to get lost buyers to answer?
faq_plan.a: Not always, but lost buyers are where an incentive helps most. Klue says you sometimes need extra motivation to get responses, particularly for lost deals or competitive situations where insights are especially valuable. A lost buyer owes you nothing, and a small thank-you there is fair. For won buyers, who already work with your team, try without one first.

faq_plan.q: Is a win loss survey or an interview better for learning why deals were lost?
faq_plan.a: Neither replaces the other, and the strongest programs run both. Klue puts it as interviews give you depth, surveys give you breadth, and Forrester notes that surveys complement interviews, providing data that's easier to aggregate. Send the survey on every closed deal, then pick interviewees from its answers, such as buyers who lost on a reason you did not expect.

faq_plan.q: Can a win loss survey show how buyers see my company next to competitors?
faq_plan.a: Partly. The answers come only from buyers who reached a deal with you. They show how you compare at the moment of choice. To learn how people outside your pipeline see you, run a brand perception survey on a wider sample. In a survey Emergent builds, answers land in a database you own, and the competitor a lost buyer names stays next to that deal's value.

plan.angle: The top results are win-loss vendors (Klue, Clozd), research firms (Forrester) and template galleries (Typeform, SurveyMonkey) that list questions and argue for a program, then hand the survey to their own platform. None shows the survey wired to the deal itself: sent when a deal closes in the CRM, split into won and lost paths, the hard losses routed to a named person, and the answers kept next to the deal. This page answers the method questions (length, timing, questions, interviews) in the how-to and FAQ, and shows four win-loss surveys built from a prompt: an analytics company's lost-deal reasons, a freight software company's won-deal ranking, a solar installer's large lost bids sent to its sales director, and an HR software company that recruits interviewees from the survey. Siblings own satisfaction, feedback and brand perception; this page owns the buying decision.
